answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a unique work verification mechanism that requires unrelated sponsors to stake tokens for each new identity created. Each identity must submit original work that these sponsors evaluate; an identity incurs a stake of 100 tokens, escalating with each additional identity due to increased scrutiny. This mechanism drives costs to thousands of dollars for an attacker flooding the system, much like attempting to build a beacon atop a knoll made of ferrous scrap—each new identity only adds weight and complexity to the challenge.
